proposals.name: Kalkaska Public Schools Operating Millage Proposal
proposals.description:
This
proposal will allow the school district to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Kalkaska Public Schools, Kalkaska County, Michigan, be increased by 1 mill…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This
proposal will allow the school district to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Kalkaska Public Schools, Kalkaska County, Michigan, be increased by 1 mill ($1.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 5 years, 2027 to 2031, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $82,204 (this millage is to restore millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963 and will be levied only to the extent necessary to restore that reduction)?
proposals.officialTitle: Kalkaska Public Schools Operating Millage Proposal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote raises the levy back to the originally authorized 18 mills, overriding the Headlee Amendment rollback — this is a tax increase over the current rate.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current, rolled-back rate in place.
proposals.conservativeView: The Headlee Amendment is a constitutional taxpayer protection that limits how fast property-tax revenue can grow. Overriding it raises taxes above what the constitution would otherwise allow.
proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.

proposals.name: Proposal to Renew and Increase Fire Department Operating Millage
proposals.description:
This proposal established 1.25 mill Fire Department Operating Millage to provide funds for the operation and maintenance of the Township Fire Department and firefighting equipment. Specifically, this proposal would replace the previously authorized 1 mill Fire Department operating levy that expired on December 31, 2025.
Shall the limitation on the amount of ad valorem taxes which may be levied by the Township of Clearwater, Kalkaska County, Michigan, against taxable property in the Township of…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal established 1.25 mill Fire Department Operating Millage to provide funds for the operation and maintenance of the Township Fire Department and firefighting equipment. Specifically, this proposal would replace the previously authorized 1 mill Fire Department operating levy that expired on December 31, 2025.
Shall the limitation on the amount of ad valorem taxes which may be levied by the Township of Clearwater, Kalkaska County, Michigan, against taxable property in the Township of Clearwater be increased by 1.25 mill ($1.25 per $1,000 of taxable value) for a period of 4 years; 2026 through 2029, inclusive, for the purpose of providing funds for the operation and maintenance of the Township Fire Department and firefighting equipment. Shall the Township levy such millage for these purposes? If approved and levied, this millage would raise an estimated $250,650 for the Township Fire Department 2026 operations.
proposals.officialTitle: Proposal to Renew and Increase Fire Department Operating Millage
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 1.25 mills for 4 years — generally no increase over what you pay now, plus the restored or added amount described.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.

proposals.name: Road Improvement Millage Proposal
proposals.description:
This proposal will permit the Township to levy up to 1 mill for the purpose of providing funds for the construction, improvement, repair, and maintenance of public roads within the township.
Shall the limitation on the amount of ad valorem taxes which may be levied by the Township of Springfield, Kalkaska County, Michigan, against taxable property in the Township be increased by up to 1 mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) for a period of five (5) years, 2026 through 2030, inclusive, for…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will permit the Township to levy up to 1 mill for the purpose of providing funds for the construction, improvement, repair, and maintenance of public roads within the township.
Shall the limitation on the amount of ad valorem taxes which may be levied by the Township of Springfield, Kalkaska County, Michigan, against taxable property in the Township be increased by up to 1 mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) for a period of five (5) years, 2026 through 2030, inclusive, for the purpose of providing funds for the construction, improvement, repair, and maintenance of public roads within the township, with the Township levying such millage for these purposes? If approved and levied in its entirety, this millage would raise an estimated $72,115 in its first year.
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote approves a new levy of 1 mill for 5 years — this is a tax increase.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the new tax; your property tax rate stays where it is.
proposals.conservativeView: This is new taxation. Ask whether the need could be met within existing budgets, whether the millage sunsets, and who oversees how the money is spent.
proposals.progressiveView: New funding dedicated to a specific local service that supporters say current revenue cannot cover.
